t.E1450.agn: In 2017 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and found no safety concern at the reported use levels. The safety of E 1450 in infant formula could not be fully assessed with the available data.
t.E1450.body: Modified starches are not absorbed intact; in the gut they are largely broken down by enzymes, and the remainder is fermented by bacteria in the large intestine.
t.E1450.eff.1.t: Its safety in infant formula could not be fully assessed with the available data
t.E1450.prod: Produced by modifying starch through a chemical reaction (modified starch).
t.E1450.pw.0: It is a source of sodium. Sodium from additives is usually less than that from salt.
t.E1450.pw.1: EFSA reported that it could not fully assess the safety of E 1450 in infant formula with the available data. In 2026 the EU required E 1450 used in infant formula to be gluten-free.
t.E1450.pw.2: EFSA reported that it could not fully assess the safety of E 1450 in infant formula with the available data. In 2026 the EU required E 1450 used in infant formula to be gluten-free.
t.E1450.regx.0: E 1450 used in infant formula and follow-on formula must be gluten-free (from 18.08.2026).
t.E1450.regx.1: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed, no safety concern at the reported uses.
t.E1450.summary: A modified starch that can disperse oil in water. It is used as an emulsifier in baby foods, flavouring emulsions and drinks.
t.E1450.what: A modified starch that can disperse oil in water; it is used as an emulsifier and stabiliser.
